# REEDHAVEN

- Project: Coastal wetland birdwatching trail
- Site area: 28,800 m²
- Boundary: 240 m east–west by 120 m north–south
- Coordinate origin: southwest corner; x east; y north; coordinate unit m
- Height reference: common site datum
- Public construction area: Visitor Margin, including supports and roof projections

## Zones

| Zone | South and north limits | Area | Surface | Shade | Public capacity |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Visitor Margin | y = 0–40 m | 9,600 m² | Existing ground and grooved timber public decking | Roof at Bird Hide; slatted canopy at Rest Deck | 36 across the two nodes |
| Habitat Buffer | y = 40–60 m | 4,800 m² | Existing wetland ground and retained reeds | Existing reeds | 0 |
| Habitat Core | y = 60–120 m | 14,400 m² | Existing mudflat and tidal creek | Open sky | 0 |

## Routes and observation nodes

- Public entrance: (0,20), surface +3.00 m
- Public route minimum clear width: 2.40 m
- Public route and observation deck level: +3.00 m
- Existing patrol boardwalk: x = 0–240 m; y = 8–11 m; clear width 3 m; deck +3.20 m
- Patrol boardwalk identity: weathered transverse timber boards, square timber posts and two horizontal timber rails
- Bird Hide: centre (80,32); footprint x = 76–84 m and y = 29–35 m; capacity 24; roof shade
- Rest Deck: centre (180,32); footprint x = 177–183 m and y = 30–34 m; capacity 12; slatted shade
- Viewing axes: x = 80 m and x = 180 m, facing north
- Sightline ground targets: y = 48 m and y = 100 m
- Eye heights above public deck: seated 1.20 m; standing 1.60 m
- Viewing screen material: stainless steel mesh

## Water and terrain

- Low tide: +0.20 m
- High tide: +1.80 m
- Ground at y = 20 m: +2.80 m
- Ground at y = 100 m: +0.20 m
- Ground difference between y = 20 m and y = 100 m: 2.60 m
- Terrain profile and creek geometry: 03-site-records.en.md

## Plants

| Code | Plant | Status | Quantity | Size or extent |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| JM | Juncus maritimus | New planting within Visitor Margin | 36 | 2 L pots |
| PM | Puccinellia maritima | New planting within Visitor Margin | 60 | 0.5 L pots |
| PA | Phragmites australis | Retained | 3 patches | 1,440 m² combined; top elevation +3.60 m |

## Fixed wording

- Site name: REEDHAVEN
- Visitor message: Watch quietly. Stay on the path.
- Observation node names: Bird Hide; Rest Deck
- Tide labels: Low tide; High tide
- Zone names: Visitor Margin; Habitat Buffer; Habitat Core

| 9 | high-tide-plan | High tide use plan | 14 | Format: PNG, 2400 by 1600 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |

steps.userMessage:
REEDHAVEN | Coastal wetland birdwatching trail

We are opening a wetland trail for birdwatchers and school groups while retaining the existing patrol boardwalk. The site is a 240 m east–west by 120 m north–south rectangle, covering 28,800 m². Coordinates start at the southwest corner, with north in the positive y direction. Visitor Margin occupies y = 0–40 m and 9,600 m²; Habitat Buffer occupies y = 40–60 m and 4,800 m²; Habitat Core occupies y = 60–120 m and 14,400 m². Public paths, supports, roofs and furniture belong entirely within Visitor Margin. Habitat Buffer and Habitat Core remain reserved for habitat management. The existing weathered timber patrol boardwalk runs across the site at y = 8–11 m, with a 3 m clear width and deck level +3.20 m.

Build the public route from the west entrance at (0,20) to two observation nodes centred at (80,32) and (180,32). Bird Hide has an 8 m by 6 m footprint, roof shade and capacity for 24 people; Rest Deck has a 6 m by 4 m footprint, slatted shade and capacity for 12 people. Public walking surfaces are +3.00 m, with a minimum clear route width of 2.40 m. Ground falls from +2.80 m at y = 20 m to +0.20 m at y = 100 m. Low tide is +0.20 m and high tide is +1.80 m, all relative to the same site datum. Retain the reed patches and their clear viewing corridors at x = 80 m and x = 180 m. The plant schedule comprises Juncus maritimus, Puccinellia maritima and retained Phragmites australis. Print "REEDHAVEN" on the masterplan, both signs, the materials and planting schedule, and the presentation; print "Watch quietly. Stay on the path." on both signs.

Audience: visiting birdwatchers, school groups and patrol staff, with the reserve team using the work to agree the route, observation facilities and daily access arrangements.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the site dimensions, public access requirements, planting quantities and fixed wording. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables, proportions, formats and stages. 03-site-records.en.md contains the coordinate boundaries, terrain profile, habitat patches and tide levels. wetland-constraints.png locates the protection bands, tidal creek, retained reeds and patrol boardwalk. wetland-section.png provides the existing ground profile and both tide levels along x = 80 m. patrol-boardwalk.png establishes the existing boardwalk's recognisable timber construction. high-tide-observation.png provides the atmosphere of quiet birdwatching beside flooded reeds. low-tide-school-group.png provides the atmosphere of a school group observing exposed mudflat.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page site analysis and zoning schedule recording the three zone names and areas, surface treatments, shade provision, public capacities, tide levels and three plant names
2. One protection and trail masterplan with north arrow, scale bar, site boundary, zone areas, planting codes, both observation footprints, public routes, patrol access and section and camera locations
3. Two terrain and observation sections, one through Bird Hide at x = 80 m and one through Rest Deck at x = 180 m, with existing ground, proposed walking levels, both tides, protection boundaries and seated and standing sightlines
4. One materials and planting schedule with the site name, three zone names and areas, three plant names, plant codes, quantities, planting sizes, retained reed extents and construction descriptions
5. Two sign designs: one entrance wayfinding sign naming Bird Hide and Rest Deck, and one interpretation panel explaining Low tide, High tide and the three recorded plants
6. Two tide-use plans of the same site, one at Low tide and one at High tide, showing water extent, public access, node capacities and the continuous patrol route
7. Two perspectives of Bird Hide and its wetland outlook, one from the southwest at High tide and one from the southeast at Low tide, with their camera positions marked on the masterplan
8. One observation-node detail sheet covering both nodes, their footprint dimensions, shade structures, seating, viewing openings and connections to the 2.40 m public route
9. One 10-second fixed-camera tide transition video from Bird Hide, moving from Low tide to High tide with both level labels
10. One presentation document of at least 8 pages, opening with the site analysis and reusing the masterplan, sections, schedule, signs, tide-use plans, perspectives and node details

Acceptance:
- The site analysis, masterplan, materials and planting schedule, and presentation repeat Visitor Margin — 9,600 m², Habitat Buffer — 4,800 m² and Habitat Core — 14,400 m²; the masterplan retains the 240 m by 120 m boundary and locates all public construction within y = 0–40 m.
- The masterplan, both tide-use plans and node detail sheet connect the entrance at (0,20) to Bird Hide at (80,32) and Rest Deck at (180,32), with public routes at least 2.40 m clear; the masterplan and tide-use plans preserve the uninterrupted 3 m patrol corridor at y = 8–11 m.
- Both sections repeat the recorded ground profile and label public surfaces +3.00 m, patrol deck +3.20 m, Low tide +0.20 m and High tide +1.80 m. Their sightlines use eye heights of 1.20 m seated and 1.60 m standing above the public deck, extending toward y = 48 m and y = 100 m through the recorded reed gaps.
- The site analysis, masterplan and materials and planting schedule repeat JM — Juncus maritimus, PM — Puccinellia maritima and PA — Phragmites australis. The masterplan and schedule locate 36 JM and 60 PM within Visitor Margin and retain the three PA patches; the schedule specifies 2 L JM, 0.5 L PM, grooved timber decking and stainless steel mesh viewing screens.
- Both signs print REEDHAVEN and Watch quietly. Stay on the path.; the entrance sign names Bird Hide and Rest Deck, and the interpretation panel labels Low tide +0.20 m and High tide +1.80 m. The masterplan, materials and planting schedule, and presentation also print REEDHAVEN.
- The node detail sheet and both perspectives retain Bird Hide at 8 m by 6 m and Rest Deck at 6 m by 4 m wherever visible. Both tide-use plans label capacities of 24 and 12 respectively; the perspectives and 10-second video match the masterplan's facilities and the sections' water levels. The presentation contains at least 8 pages and repeats the site analysis's three zone areas and both tide levels.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
